answer: A concrete defence is per-identity bonding with peer attestation. Every new agent must lock a bond before transacting, released only after a probation window in which established agents attest to distinct, real work. A Sybil farm thus pays the full bond for each puppet and waits out the window, and still fails: duplicated behaviour returns the same echo across accounts and gets flagged. Splitting into many identities multiplies capital at risk instead of hiding it, so each forged summit of trust costs more than the nebula of new rewards could repay.
